reference.title: Development of bifunctional biosensors for sensing and dynamic control of glycolysis flux in metabolic engineering

target.condition: Calibration via extracellular FBP addition 0.001-400 mM with 10 g/L acetate (Fig. 2D); other conditions unknown

trigger.observation: A single fixed biosensor design cannot cover the in vivo FBP range for diverse flux-switch scenarios; varying promoter/TF/TFBS parameters was expected to shift threshold and dynamic range
trigger.reasoning: Construct and tune positive-response (activating) FBP/Cra biosensors and characterize dose-response behavior
trigger.source_location: E. coli (host strain for biosensor characterization not fully specified in available text; requires Methods)

evidence.source_location: CK- (no plasmid pL18), CK (0 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP), '0' (10 g/L acetate, 0 mM FBP)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Dose-response curves of constructed variants were experimentally measured and Hill-fitted (Fig. 2)
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Promoter architecture variants (pL01-pL10); tuning via Cra overexpression and Cra ligand-binding-affinity modification (pL15-pL18); kinetic parameters from Hill fits

result.metric: Fluorescence; dose-response curves; EC50 and dynamic range
result.after: Positive-response biosensors with tunable thresholds/dynamic ranges obtained (pL15-pL18 characterized)

decision_chain.rule: Biosensor threshold and dynamic range can be rationally tuned by adjusting core promoter strength, TFBS position, TF-box sequence affinity, TF expression level, and TF-ligand binding affinity.

trigger.observation: Need for repressing-type sensors with distinct thresholds to drive dynamic downregulation of glycolysis (pfkA) in later applications
trigger.reasoning: Construct and tune negative-response (repressing) FBP/Cra biosensors

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Mutant sensors characterized experimentally by dose-response curves (Fig. 3B, 3C)
decision_chain.implementation_detail: Promoter variants pL19-pL30; pL35 = Cra with amino acid mutations at sites 57, 58, 59, 60 expressed from P23102, altering ligand affinity

result.after: Negative-response biosensors pL19, pL25, pL35 with defined kinetic parameters; pL19 linear FBP detection range ~0-50 mmol/g DCW (Supplementary Fig. 3C)

decision_chain.rule: Altering the ligand-binding affinity of the transcription factor (e.g., Cra) by protein mutation shifts biosensor threshold/dynamic range without changing promoter architecture.

trigger.observation: Permanent pfkA deletion in the EP-bifido strain gave 64.3 mol% yield but only 11.02 g/L MVA because growth and glucose uptake were severely suppressed; a timed (dynamic) rather than permanent block of glycolysis was needed
trigger.reasoning: Dynamically control glycolysis flux in the EP-bifido pathway for high MVA production

evidence.source_location: Nonregulated BW-Pzwf::P23109; benchmark: prior static BW-delta-pfkA (11.02 g/L, 64.3 mol% yield) and prior IPTG-CRISPRi pfkA suppression (8.53 g/L, Li et al. 2021 - background_citation)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Trigger and outcome are measured titers/yields/growth from this lab's prior and current experiments

alternatives.approach: Static permanent pfkA knockout (prior EP-bifido design) - abandoned due to growth/glucose-uptake suppression
IPTG-induced CRISPRi suppression of pfkA (Li et al. 2021, 8.53 g/L) - outperformed by autonomous FBP sensing; not retested here

decision_chain.implementation_detail: Step 1: genomic zwf promoter replaced with stronger promoter P23109 to enhance PP pathway flux. Step 2: genomic pfkA promoter replaced by negative-response biosensor promoters Ppam (pL19, -> BW-PMT) or Ppar (pL25, -> BW-PR), creating the dynamic EP-bifido pathway. Step 3: BW-PR cultivated in 1-L fermenter

result.metric: Cell growth; MVA titer and mol% carbon yield; acetate/byproducts; pfkA mRNA; intracellular FBP; glucose uptake
result.after: BW-PR: 73.31 g/L MVA, 63.00 mol% yield, <0.1 g/L acetate, stationary phase ~12 h, FBP drop after 15 h, reduced pfkA mRNA; 1-L fermenter: 111.3 g/L MVA at 120 h, no by-products. BW-PMT <2.47 g/L acetate

decision_chain.rule: When static knockout of an essential glycolytic step causes severe growth defects, replace it with metabolite-responsive dynamic repression to temporally uncouple cell growth from production.

target.condition: Shake-flask GlcNAc fermentation with glucose as sole carbon source; details unknown (Methods missing)

trigger.observation: F6P is a competitive precursor between glycolysis and GlcNAc synthesis, so pfkA had to be downregulated and glmS upregulated; early-stage glmS overexpression causes cell lysis and growth inhibition (Deng et al. 2005), motivating delayed, sensor-driven activation
trigger.reasoning: Dual dynamic regulation of glycolysis flux and GlcNAc biosynthesis
trigger.source_location: DN5 (modified DH5alpha: nag, ackA, poxB, ldhA, nan knocked out; constructed in prior lab studies)

evidence.source_location: DN5 without dynamic regulation (0.46 g/L GlcNAc)

decision_chain.evidence_grading_rationale: 模型自评(硬): 见 ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale——需人工确认 | Titers, growth and FBP measured in this study; the lysis risk of early glmS overexpression is literature-reported, not re-measured here
decision_chain.implementation_detail: pfkA promoter replaced with Ppam/Ppar (DN5-IM, DN5-PM); glmS placed under positive-response promoters PM23107 (pBacm) and PR23107-cra plus cra-P23102 (pBacar) in DN5 (DN5-GM, DN5-GAR); combined regulation by transforming pBacm/pBacar into DN5-IM (DN5-IMM, DN5-IMAR)

result.metric: Cell growth; glucose consumption; GlcNAc titer; intracellular FBP
result.after: DN5-IM 8.65 g/L; DN5-GM 6.33 g/L; DN5-GAR 7.98 g/L; DN5-IMM 8.63 g/L GlcNAc; dual regulation did not obviously exceed single regulation; FBP decreased in pfkA-repressed strains, unchanged in glmS-activated strain

decision_chain.rule: For products whose precursor competes with glycolysis, pair dynamic repression of the competing glycolytic step with delayed dynamic activation of the product-forming enzyme when early constitutive expression of that enzyme is growth-toxic.

engineering_problem.problem_statement: Design and construct bifunctional glycolysis-flux biosensors based on the FBP-Cra regulatory pair that sense intracellular fructose-1,6-diphosphate (FBP) as a proxy for glycolysis flux, tune them for varied thresholds/dynamic ranges, and use them for dynamic control of glycolysis flux to improve production of mevalonate (MVA) and N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc) in E. coli.
